body: When blurred, the standard Kazakh licence plates are mostly white with a small hint of blue on the left side.

Kazakhstan uses both Cyrillic and Latin alphabets, with Russian sometimes used monolingually. The Kazakh alphabet contains unique letters such as Ә (Ä), Ғ (Ǵ), Қ (Q), Ң (Ń), Ө (Ö), Ұ (W), Ү (Ü), Һ (H), І (I) and the Latin text can resemble Turkish.
All coverage in Kazakhstan was captured with a white pickup truck, sometimes partially blurred.
Kazakhstan features diverse landscapes including deserts, grassy steppes, mountain passes, and birch forests, with rural coverage mostly flat and open.
Infrastructure like pedestrian signs, poles, houses, and bollards in Kazakhstan closely resembles that in Russia.
Pedestrian crossings use yellow and white stripes with white dashes on either side, unlike Russia which lacks the dashes.
Kazakhstan uses varied post-Soviet style bollards and unique thin bollards attached at a 90° angle, found only in Kazakhstan.
Tree trunks are frequently painted white at the bottom, common also in parts of Russia.
Kazakhstan primarily uses yellow and black chevrons, except at T intersections where red and white chevrons appear.
Gas pipes are very common in Kazakh cities.
The koshkar-muiz ornamental pattern is found in various decorations across Kazakhstan.
Many Kazakh towns have intricate entrance arches as distinctive features.
Coverage in Kazakhstan focuses on major roads and cities; rural roads have less coverage.
Kazakhstan's coverage regions correspond to seasons: summer in west/central, autumn in northeast, winter in southeast.
Driving directions signage is helpful to narrow down rural locations.
Area codes in Kazakhstan follow an east-to-west pattern on three horizontal lines.
Licence plate codes on trucks and buses follow an alphabetic order aligned with region names; smaller numbers correlate with earlier starting letters.
Reading letters under QR codes on street signs can indicate regions, though this is rare.
Kazakhstan's mostly flat terrain means spotting hills or mountains (e.g., Karaganda, Aktobe, south/east) helps localize areas.
Northern Kazakhstan has lush birch forests and green fields, resembling landscapes in Russia's Omsk Oblast.
Expansive grassy plains are typical in northwestern Kazakhstan, especially Akmola and Kostanay.
Southwestern Kazakhstan features sandy, shrubby desert-like landscapes.
Tall, often snow-capped mountains appear in southeastern Kazakhstan.
East Kazakhstan has hilly, forested fall-colored landscapes; Ridder town is flat but surrounded by hazy mountains.
Snow coverage is found in southeast Kazakhstan, especially east of Almaty.
Southern Kazakhstan near Uzbekistan has dry, shrubby orange grass hills and flat agricultural land near Zhetisay with distinctive red and white KM markers.
Grassy rolling hills are common just north of Bishkek in southern Kazakhstan.
Around Semey, you will find pine forests and deciduous trees with fall colors.
The divided E38 highway runs southeast to northwest from Shymkent to Kyzylorda through green and dry sandy landscapes.
The M36 from Karaganda to Almaty is often under construction with yellow lines; the landscape is a dry orange-brown steppe.
M36 between Karaganda and Astana is divided highway with grassy, occasionally hilly steppes and yellow outer lines.
P4/A17 from Astana to Pavlodar traverses less vegetated hilly steppe landscapes with yellow outer lines.
Roads from Kyzylagash to Druzhba have a unique hazy, dead hilly landscape with small mountains to the south or east.
The A26 from Kandyagash to M32/E38 is very poor quality with mostly unpaved sections, flat semi-arid grassy plains, and cloudy weather.
The A1 from Astana to Shchuchinsk is a 6-lane divided highway with green trees and grassy plains or hills.
The A17 to Ulytau features poor pavement, a white middle line, grassy steppe, and some fall-colored trees.
North of Zhezqazghan has no road lines, a dry desolate hilly landscape with red or orange soil and sunny weather with cumulus clouds.
R260 road is mostly paved with cracks and lack of lines; landscape is slightly hilly steppe with yellow grass and reddish soil; R217 is better maintained.

Most useful pole paints: West Kazakhstan (red, white, black), Atyrau (blue, white, black), Akmola (red thin, white, black), Kostanay (turquoise, yellow), Petropavl (white, light grey), Taraz (red, yellow, black), Kyzylorda (yellow/red/white), Kyzylorda lamp posts (white/turquoise).

Other useful pole paints: Rudny (red, yellow, red, white), Kokshetau (light blue bottom, yellow stripes), Shchuchinsk (red, yellow), Ekibastuz (blue, white), Shymkent (yellow, red, green), Kentau (blue, yellow, red, blue, black).
Bus stops: Atyrau (modern white/neon green), Kostanay (brown with blue/yellow crest), Petropavl (brown glass), Karaganda (turquoise curved roof), Zhezqazghan (wide blue indoor/outdoor sections).

Buses: Aktobe (orange/black), Zhezqazghan (orange/white with "Men ♥ Jezz/Zhez"), Astana (white/black/green electric), Karaganda (turquoise), Semey (light green/white), Almaty (green with white patterns), Taraz (similar to Almaty with name).
Building-attached street signs vary: Aktobe (compact with QR code), Petropavl (white with blue semicircle), Astana (generic design), Zhetisay (generic but absent in Turkistan/Shymkent).
Yellow boxes connected to gas pipes are common outside houses in Shymkent, Turkistan, and Taldykorgan.
Turkistan features thin grey lamps with two small light sources near the end.
Kulsary lamps have a large blue photocell on top.
Some Uralsk lamps have three lamps arranged in ascending height.
A visible wire at the back of the Street View car is common in western Kazakhstan.
Three-dot pattern with two close together at the rear roof and one above left is found north of Zhezqazghan.
Near Kyzylorda, a three-dot pattern appears with one bottom right and two side by side near middle.
Zigzag smudge on left car side can be seen on the P24 between Oskemen and Semey.
Dirty roof back is visible east of Almaty, similar dirt seen in nearby cities.
Small smudge left bottom roof between Petropavl and Kokshetau.
Thin dirt and dust coating near roof back between Kokshetau and Atbasar.
Vertical line of dirt appears on the right roof side east of Aktobe.
Faint dot on middle-right of roof south of Beyneu, accompanied by nearby smudges.
Dense Baltic pine forests north of Shchuchinsk, north of Astana; Baltic pines appear in other areas too.
Parts of Oskemen exhibit hazy forest fire coverage.
Snow coverage in mountains in southern Almaty city.
Altyn Emel National Park: barren grassland surrounded by snowy mountains, with some areas very snowy and a small curvy mountain pass in the east.
May coverage only in Almaty exclave of Alataou; sunny with visible southern mountains.
A small ridge of hills visible to the north in Taldykorgan coverage.
Near Turkmenistan border, southwestern Kazakhstan has an unpaved sandy desert road with very bright sand landscape.
